  1206→// Main entry point for the CLI
  1207→func main() {
  1208→	// Parse critical flags early by manually checking os.Args
  1209→	// This is necessary because cobra's ParseFlags doesn't work correctly before subcommands are added
  1210→	args := os.Args[1:]
  1211→	for i := 0; i < len(args); i++ {
  1212→		arg := args[i]
  1213→		switch arg {
  1214→		case "--no-usage-analytics":
  1215→			noAnalytics = true
  1216→		case "--console":
  1217→			console = true
  1218→		case "--log":
  1219→			logFile = true
  1220→		case "--debug":
  1221→			debug = true
  1222→		case "--silent":
  1223→			silent = true
  1224→		case "--no-version-check":
  1225→			noVersionCheck = true
  1226→		case "--no-telemetry-prompts":
  1227→			noTelemetryPrompts = true
  1228→		case "--output-dir":
  1229→			// Handle --output-dir <value> format (space-separated)
  1230→			if i+1 < len(args) && !strings.HasPrefix(args[i+1], "-") {
  1231→				outputDir = utils.ExpandTilde(args[i+1])
  1232→				i++ // Skip the value in next iteration
  1233→			}
  1234→		case "--telemetry-endpoint":
  1235→			if i+1 < len(args) && !strings.HasPrefix(args[i+1], "-") {
  1236→				telemetryEndpoint = args[i+1]
  1237→				i++ // Skip the value in next iteration
  1238→			}
  1239→		case "--telemetry-service-name":
  1240→			// Handle --telemetry-service-name <value> format (space-separated)
  1241→			if i+1 < len(args) && !strings.HasPrefix(args[i+1], "-") {
  1242→				telemetryServiceName = args[i+1]
  1243→				i++ // Skip the value in next iteration
  1244→			}
  1245→		case "--debug-dir":
  1246→			// Handle --debug-dir <value> format (space-separated)
  1247→			if i+1 < len(args) && !strings.HasPrefix(args[i+1], "-") {
  1248→				debugDir = utils.ExpandTilde(args[i+1])
  1249→				i++ // Skip the value in next iteration
  1250→			}
  1251→		case "--local-time-zone":
  1252→			localTimeZone = true
  1253→		}
  1254→		// Handle --output-dir=value format
  1255→		if strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--output-dir=") {
  1256→			outputDir = utils.ExpandTilde(strings.TrimPrefix(arg, "--output-dir="))
  1257→		}
  1258→		// Handle --debug-dir=value format
  1259→		if strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--debug-dir=") {
  1260→			debugDir = utils.ExpandTilde(strings.TrimPrefix(arg, "--debug-dir="))
  1261→		}
  1262→		// Handle --telemetry-endpoint=value format
  1263→		if strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--telemetry-endpoint=") {
  1264→			telemetryEndpoint = strings.TrimPrefix(arg, "--telemetry-endpoint=")
  1265→		}
  1266→		// Handle --telemetry-service-name=value format
  1267→		if strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--telemetry-service-name=") {
  1268→			telemetryServiceName = strings.TrimPrefix(arg, "--telemetry-service-name=")
  1269→		}
  1270→	}
  1271→
  1272→	// Load configuration early (before logging setup) so TOML settings can affect logging
  1273→	// Priority: CLI flags > local project config > user-level config
  1274→	// Note: OTEL_* env vars take highest priority for telemetry
  1275→	cfg, cfgErr := config.Load(&config.CLIOverrides{
  1276→		OutputDir:            outputDir,
  1277→		LocalTimeZone:        localTimeZone,
  1278→		NoVersionCheck:       noVersionCheck,
  1279→		NoCloudSync:          noCloudSync,
  1280→		OnlyCloudSync:        onlyCloudSync,
  1281→		DebugDir:             debugDir,
  1282→		Console:              console,
  1283→		Log:                  logFile,
  1284→		Debug:                debug,
  1285→		Silent:               silent,
  1286→		NoAnalytics:          noAnalytics,
  1287→		TelemetryEndpoint:    telemetryEndpoint,
  1288→		TelemetryServiceName: telemetryServiceName,
  1289→		NoTelemetryPrompts:   noTelemetryPrompts,
  1290→	})
  1291→	if cfgErr != nil {
  1292→		// Use fallback empty config if load fails - will log error after logging is set up
  1293→		cfg = &config.Config{}
  1294→	}
  1295→	// Store config for use by command functions (e.g., provider commands in run)
  1296→	loadedConfig = cfg
  1297→
  1298→	// Apply config values to flag variables so the rest of the code can use them unchanged.
  1299→	// This merges TOML config with CLI flags (CLI flags take precedence via config.Load).
  1300→	if cfg.GetOutputDir() != "" {
  1301→		outputDir = utils.ExpandTilde(cfg.GetOutputDir())
  1302→	}
  1303→	if cfg.GetDebugDir() != "" {
  1304→		debugDir = utils.ExpandTilde(cfg.GetDebugDir())
  1305→	}
  1306→	localTimeZone = cfg.IsLocalTimeZoneEnabled()
  1307→	noVersionCheck = !cfg.IsVersionCheckEnabled()
  1308→	noCloudSync = !cfg.IsCloudSyncEnabled()
  1309→	onlyCloudSync = !cfg.IsLocalSyncEnabled()
  1310→	noAnalytics = !cfg.IsAnalyticsEnabled()
  1311→	console = cfg.IsConsoleEnabled()
  1312→	logFile = cfg.IsLogEnabled()
  1313→	debug = cfg.IsDebugEnabled()
  1314→	silent = cfg.IsSilentEnabled()
  1315→
  1316→	noTelemetryPrompts = noTelemetryPrompts || cfg.IsTelemetryPromptsDisabled()
  1317→
  1318→	// Set SPI debug dir override before any commands run
  1319→	if debugDir != "" {
  1320→		spi.SetDebugBaseDir(debugDir)
  1321→	}
  1322→
  1323→	// Set up logging early before creating commands (which access the registry)
  1324→	if console || logFile {
  1325→		var logPath string
  1326→		if logFile {
  1327→			config, _ := utils.SetupOutputConfig(outputDir, debugDir)
  1328→			logPath = config.GetLogPath()
  1329→		}
  1330→		_ = log.SetupLogger(console, logFile, debug, logPath)
  1331→	} else {
  1332→		// Set up discard logger to prevent default slog output
  1333→		_ = log.SetupLogger(false, false, false, "")
  1334→	}
  1335→
  1336→	// NOW create the commands - after logging is configured
  1337→	rootCmd = createRootCommand()
  1338→	runCmd = createRunCommand()
  1339→	watchCmd := cmdpkg.CreateWatchCommand(&cloudURL, localTimeZone, debugDir)
  1340→	syncCmd = createSyncCommand()
  1341→	listCmd := cmdpkg.CreateListCommand()
  1342→	checkCmd := cmdpkg.CreateCheckCommand()
  1343→	versionCmd := cmdpkg.CreateVersionCommand(version)
  1344→	loginCmd := cmdpkg.CreateLoginCommand(&cloudURL)
  1345→	logoutCmd := cmdpkg.CreateLogoutCommand(&cloudURL)
  1346→
  1347→	// Set version for the automatic version flag
  1348→	rootCmd.Version = version
  1349→
  1350→	// Override the default version template to match our version command output
  1351→	rootCmd.SetVersionTemplate("{{.Version}} (SpecStory)")
  1352→
  1353→	// Set our custom help command (for "specstory help")
  1354→	helpCmd := cmdpkg.CreateHelpCommand(rootCmd)
  1355→	rootCmd.SetHelpCommand(helpCmd)
  1356→
  1357→	// Add the subcommands
  1358→	rootCmd.AddCommand(runCmd)
  1359→	rootCmd.AddCommand(watchCmd)
  1360→	rootCmd.AddCommand(syncCmd)
  1361→	rootCmd.AddCommand(listCmd)
  1362→	rootCmd.AddCommand(versionCmd)
  1363→	rootCmd.AddCommand(checkCmd)
  1364→	rootCmd.AddCommand(loginCmd)
  1365→	rootCmd.AddCommand(logoutCmd)
  1366→
  1367→	// Global flags available on all commands
  1368→	// Use current variable values as defaults so config file values are preserved
  1369→	rootCmd.PersistentFlags().BoolVar(&console, "console", console, "enable error/warn/info output to stdout")
  1370→	rootCmd.PersistentFlags().BoolVar(&logFile, "log", logFile, "write error/warn/info output to ./.specstory/debug/debug.log")
  1371→	rootCmd.PersistentFlags().BoolVar(&debug, "debug", debug, "enable debug-level output (requires --console or --log)")
  1372→	rootCmd.PersistentFlags().BoolVar(&noAnalytics, "no-usage-analytics", noAnalytics, "disable usage analytics")
  1373→	rootCmd.PersistentFlags().BoolVar(&silent, "silent", silent, "suppress all non-error output")
  1374→	rootCmd.PersistentFlags().BoolVar(&noVersionCheck, "no-version-check", noVersionCheck, "skip checking for newer versions")
  1375→	rootCmd.PersistentFlags().StringVar(&cloudToken, "cloud-token", "", "use a SpecStory Cloud refresh token for this session (bypasses login)")
  1376→	_ = rootCmd.PersistentFlags().MarkHidden("cloud-token") // Hidden flag
  1377→
  1378→	// Command-specific flags
  1379→	syncCmd.Flags().StringSliceP("session", "s", []string{}, "optional session IDs to sync (can be specified multiple times, provider-specific format)")
  1380→	syncCmd.Flags().BoolVar(&printToStdout, "print", printToStdout, "output session markdown to stdout instead of saving (requires -s flag)")
  1381→	syncCmd.Flags().StringVar(&outputDir, "output-dir", outputDir, "custom output directory for markdown files (default: ./.specstory/history)")
  1382→	syncCmd.Flags().StringVar(&debugDir, "debug-dir", debugDir, "custom output directory for debug data (default: ./.specstory/debug)")
  1383→	syncCmd.Flags().BoolVar(&noCloudSync, "no-cloud-sync", noCloudSync, "disable cloud sync functionality")
  1384→	syncCmd.Flags().BoolVar(&onlyCloudSync, "only-cloud-sync", onlyCloudSync, "skip local markdown file saves, only upload to cloud (requires authentication)")
  1385→	syncCmd.Flags().StringVar(&cloudURL, "cloud-url", "", "override the default cloud API base URL")
  1386→	_ = syncCmd.Flags().MarkHidden("cloud-url") // Hidden flag
  1387→	syncCmd.Flags().Bool("debug-raw", false, "debug mode to output pretty-printed raw data files")
  1388→	_ = syncCmd.Flags().MarkHidden("debug-raw") // Hidden flag
  1389→	syncCmd.Flags().BoolVar(&localTimeZone, "local-time-zone", localTimeZone, "use local timezone for file name and content timestamps (when not present: UTC)")
  1390→	syncCmd.Flags().StringVar(&telemetryEndpoint, "telemetry-endpoint", "", "Open Telemetry Protocol (OTLP) gRPC collector endpoint (default is off, e.g., localhost:4317)")
  1391→	syncCmd.Flags().StringVar(&telemetryServiceName, "telemetry-service-name", "", "override the default service name for telemetry, if telemetry is enabled")
  1392→	syncCmd.Flags().BoolVar(&noTelemetryPrompts, "no-telemetry-prompts", noTelemetryPrompts, "exclude prompt text from telemetry spans, if telemetry is enabled")
  1393→
  1394→	runCmd.Flags().BoolVar(&provenanceEnabled, "provenance", false, "enable AI provenance tracking (correlate file changes to agent activity)")
  1395→	_ = runCmd.Flags().MarkHidden("provenance") // Hidden flag
  1396→	runCmd.Flags().StringP("command", "c", "", "custom agent execution command for the provider")
  1397→	runCmd.Flags().String("resume", "", "resume a specific session by ID")
  1398→	runCmd.Flags().StringVar(&outputDir, "output-dir", outputDir, "custom output directory for markdown files (default: ./.specstory/history)")
  1399→	runCmd.Flags().StringVar(&debugDir, "debug-dir", debugDir, "custom output directory for debug data (default: ./.specstory/debug)")
  1400→	runCmd.Flags().BoolVar(&noCloudSync, "no-cloud-sync", noCloudSync, "disable cloud sync functionality")
  1401→	runCmd.Flags().BoolVar(&onlyCloudSync, "only-cloud-sync", onlyCloudSync, "skip local markdown file saves, only upload to cloud (requires authentication)")
  1402→	runCmd.Flags().StringVar(&cloudURL, "cloud-url", "", "override the default cloud API base URL")
  1403→	_ = runCmd.Flags().MarkHidden("cloud-url") // Hidden flag
  1404→	runCmd.Flags().Bool("debug-raw", false, "debug mode to output pretty-printed raw data files")
  1405→	_ = runCmd.Flags().MarkHidden("debug-raw") // Hidden flag
  1406→	runCmd.Flags().BoolVar(&localTimeZone, "local-time-zone", localTimeZone, "use local timezone for file name and content timestamps (when not present: UTC)")
  1407→	runCmd.Flags().StringVar(&telemetryEndpoint, "telemetry-endpoint", "", "Open Telemetry Protocol (OTLP) gRPC collector endpoint (default is off, e.g., localhost:4317)")
  1408→	runCmd.Flags().StringVar(&telemetryServiceName, "telemetry-service-name", "", "override the default service name for telemetry, if telemetry is enabled")
  1409→	runCmd.Flags().BoolVar(&noTelemetryPrompts, "no-telemetry-prompts", noTelemetryPrompts, "exclude prompt text from telemetry spans, if telemetry is enabled")
  1410→
  1411→	// Initialize analytics with the full CLI command (unless disabled)
  1412→	slog.Debug("Analytics initialization check", "noAnalytics", noAnalytics, "flag_should_disable", noAnalytics)
  1413→	if !noAnalytics {
  1414→		slog.Debug("Initializing analytics")
  1415→		fullCommand := strings.Join(os.Args, " ")
  1416→		if err := analytics.Init(fullCommand, version); err != nil {
  1417→			// Log error but don't fail - analytics should not break the app
  1418→			slog.Warn("Failed to initialize analytics", "error", err)
  1419→		}
  1420→		defer func() { _ = analytics.Close() }() // Analytics errors shouldn't break the app
  1421→	} else {
  1422→		slog.Debug("Analytics disabled by --no-usage-analytics flag")
  1423→	}
  1424→
  1425→	// Log config load error after logging is set up
  1426→	if cfgErr != nil {
  1427→		slog.Warn("Failed to load config file, using defaults", "error", cfgErr)
  1428→	}
  1429→
  1430→	// Initialize telemetry (after logging is configured)
  1431→	if err := telemetry.Init(context.Background(), telemetry.Options{
  1432→		ServiceName: cfg.GetTelemetryServiceName(),
  1433→		Endpoint:    cfg.GetTelemetryEndpoint(),
  1434→		Enabled:     cfg.IsTelemetryEnabled(),
  1435→	}); err != nil {
  1436→		slog.Warn("Failed to initialize telemetry", "error", err)
  1437→	}
  1438→	// Shutdown flushes pending spans/metrics before closing providers.
  1439→	defer func() {
  1440→		shutdownCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
  1441→		defer cancel()
  1442→		if err := telemetry.Shutdown(shutdownCtx); err != nil {
  1443→			slog.Warn("Failed to shutdown telemetry", "error", err)
  1444→		}
  1445→	}()
  1446→
  1447→	// Check for updates (blocking)
  1448→	utils.CheckForUpdates(version, noVersionCheck, silent)
  1449→
  1450→	// Ensure proper cleanup and logging on exit
  1451→	defer func() {
  1452→		if r := recover(); r != nil {
  1453→			slog.Error("=== SpecStory PANIC ===", "panic", r)
  1454→			// Still try to wait for cloud sync even on panic
  1455→			_ = cloud.Shutdown(cloud.CloudSyncTimeout)
  1456→			log.CloseLogger()
  1457→			panic(r) // Re-panic after logging
  1458→		}
  1459→		// Wait for cloud sync operations to complete before exiting
  1460→		cloudStats := cloud.Shutdown(cloud.CloudSyncTimeout)
  1461→
  1462→		// Track cloud sync analytics if we have stats
  1463→		if cloudStats != nil {
  1464→			// Calculate total attempted (all sessions that started sync)
  1465→			totalCloudSessions := cloudStats.SessionsAttempted
  1466→
  1467→			// Track cloud sync completion event
  1468→			if cloudStats.SessionsUpdated > 0 || cloudStats.SessionsCreated > 0 || cloudStats.SessionsErrored > 0 || cloudStats.SessionsTimedOut > 0 {
  1469→				analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventCloudSyncComplete, analytics.Properties{
  1470→					"sessions_created":   cloudStats.SessionsCreated,
  1471→					"sessions_updated":   cloudStats.SessionsUpdated,
  1472→					"sessions_skipped":   cloudStats.SessionsSkipped,
  1473→					"sessions_errored":   cloudStats.SessionsErrored,
  1474→					"sessions_timed_out": cloudStats.SessionsTimedOut,
  1475→					"total":              totalCloudSessions,
  1476→				})
  1477→			}
  1478→
  1479→			// Display cloud sync stats if not in silent mode
  1480→			if !silent && totalCloudSessions > 0 {
  1481→				fmt.Println() // Visual separation from provider sync output
  1482→
  1483→				// Determine if sync was complete or incomplete based on errors/timeouts
  1484→				if cloudStats.SessionsErrored > 0 || cloudStats.SessionsTimedOut > 0 {
  1485→					fmt.Printf("❌ Cloud sync incomplete! 📊 %s%d%s %s processed\n",
  1486→						log.ColorBoldCyan, totalCloudSessions, log.ColorReset, pluralSession(int(totalCloudSessions)))
  1487→				} else {
  1488→					fmt.Printf("☁️  Cloud sync complete! 📊 %s%d%s %s processed\n",
  1489→						log.ColorBoldCyan, totalCloudSessions, log.ColorReset, pluralSession(int(totalCloudSessions)))
  1490→				}
  1491→				fmt.Println()
  1492→
  1493→				fmt.Printf("  ⏭️ %s%d %s up to date (skipped)%s\n",
  1494→					log.ColorCyan, cloudStats.SessionsSkipped, pluralSession(int(cloudStats.SessionsSkipped)), log.ColorReset)
  1495→				fmt.Printf("  ♻️ %s%d %s updated%s\n",
  1496→					log.ColorYellow, cloudStats.SessionsUpdated, pluralSession(int(cloudStats.SessionsUpdated)), log.ColorReset)
  1497→				fmt.Printf("  ✨ %s%d new %s created%s\n",
  1498→					log.ColorGreen, cloudStats.SessionsCreated, pluralSession(int(cloudStats.SessionsCreated)), log.ColorReset)
  1499→
  1500→				// Only show errors if there were any
  1501→				if cloudStats.SessionsErrored > 0 {
  1502→					fmt.Printf("  ❌ %s%d %s errored%s\n",
  1503→						log.ColorRed, cloudStats.SessionsErrored, pluralSession(int(cloudStats.SessionsErrored)), log.ColorReset)
  1504→				}
  1505→
  1506→				// Only show timed out sessions if there were any
  1507→				if cloudStats.SessionsTimedOut > 0 {
  1508→					fmt.Printf("  ⏱️  %s%d %s timed out%s\n",
  1509→						log.ColorRed, cloudStats.SessionsTimedOut, pluralSession(int(cloudStats.SessionsTimedOut)), log.ColorReset)
  1510→				}
  1511→				fmt.Println()
  1512→
  1513→				// Display link to SpecStory Cloud (deep link to session if from run command)
  1514→				cwd, cwdErr := os.Getwd()
  1515→				if cwdErr == nil {
  1516→					identityManager := utils.NewProjectIdentityManager(cwd)
  1517→					if projectID, err := identityManager.GetProjectID(); err == nil {
  1518→						fmt.Printf("💡 Search and chat with your AI conversation history at:\n")
  1519→						if lastRunSessionID != "" {
  1520→							// Deep link to the specific session from run command
  1521→							fmt.Printf("   %shttps://cloud.specstory.com/projects/%s/sessions/%s%s\n\n",
  1522→								log.ColorBoldCyan, projectID, lastRunSessionID, log.ColorReset)
  1523→						} else {
  1524→							// Link to project overview for sync command
  1525→							fmt.Printf("   %shttps://cloud.specstory.com/projects/%s%s\n\n",
  1526→								log.ColorBoldCyan, projectID, log.ColorReset)
  1527→						}
  1528→					}
  1529→				}
  1530→			}
  1531→		}
  1532→
  1533→		if console || logFile {
  1534→			slog.Info("=== SpecStory Exiting ===", "code", 0, "status", "normal termination")
  1535→		}
  1536→		log.CloseLogger()
  1537→	}()
  1538→
  1539→	if err := fang.Execute(context.Background(), rootCmd, fang.WithVersion(version)); err != nil {
  1540→		// Check if we're running the check command by looking at the executed command
  1541→		executedCmd, _, _ := rootCmd.Find(os.Args[1:])
  1542→		if executedCmd == checkCmd {
  1543→			if console || logFile {
  1544→				slog.Error("=== SpecStory Exiting ===", "code", 2, "status", "agent execution failure")
  1545→				slog.Error("Error", "error", err)
  1546→			}
  1547→			// For check command, the error details are handled by checkSingleProvider/checkAllProviders
  1548→			// So we just exit silently here
  1549→			_ = cloud.Shutdown(cloud.CloudSyncTimeout)
  1550→			os.Exit(2)
  1551→		} else {
  1552→			if console || logFile {
  1553→				slog.Error("=== SpecStory Exiting ===", "code", 1, "status", "error")
  1554→				slog.Error("Error", "error", err)
  1555→			}
  1556→			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr) // Visual separation makes error output more noticeable
  1557→
  1558→			// Only show usage for actual command/flag errors from Cobra
  1559→			// These are errors like "unknown command", "unknown flag", "invalid argument", etc.
  1560→			// For all other errors (authentication, network, file system, etc.), we should NOT show usage
  1561→			errMsg := err.Error()
  1562→			isCommandError := strings.Contains(errMsg, "unknown command") ||
  1563→				strings.Contains(errMsg, "unknown flag") ||
  1564→				strings.Contains(errMsg, "invalid argument") ||
  1565→				strings.Contains(errMsg, "required flag") ||
  1566→				strings.Contains(errMsg, "accepts") || // e.g., "accepts 1 arg(s), received 2"
  1567→				strings.Contains(errMsg, "no such flag") ||
  1568→				strings.Contains(errMsg, "flag needs an argument")
  1569→
  1570→			if isCommandError {
  1571→				_ = rootCmd.Usage() // Ignore error; we're exiting anyway
  1572→				fmt.Println()       // Add visual separation after usage for better CLI readability
  1573→			}
  1574→			_ = cloud.Shutdown(cloud.CloudSyncTimeout)
  1575→			os.Exit(1)
  1576→		}
  1577→	}
  1578→}
  1579→

    87→// parseResourceAttributes parses OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES env var into attribute.KeyValue slice.
    88→// Format: "key1=value1,key2=value2"
    89→func parseResourceAttributes() []attribute.KeyValue {
    90→	envVal := os.Getenv("OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES")
    91→	if envVal == "" {
    92→		return nil
    93→	}
    94→
    95→	var attrs []attribute.KeyValue
    96→	pairs := strings.Split(envVal, ",")
    97→	for _, pair := range pairs {
    98→		pair = strings.TrimSpace(pair)
    99→		if pair == "" {
   100→			continue
   101→		}
   102→		kv := strings.SplitN(pair, "=", 2)
   103→		if len(kv) == 2 {
   104→			key := strings.TrimSpace(kv[0])
   105→			value := strings.TrimSpace(kv[1])
   106→			if key != "" {
   107→				attrs = append(attrs, attribute.String(key, value))
   108→			}
   109→		}
   110→	}
   111→	return attrs
   112→}

   114→// parseEndpoint normalises an OTLP endpoint string into a bare host:port suitable
   115→// for otlptracegrpc.WithEndpoint and a flag indicating whether TLS should be disabled.
   116→//
   117→// Accepted formats:
   118→//
   119→//	"localhost:4317"              → host="localhost:4317",  insecure=true
   120→//	"http://localhost:4317"       → host="localhost:4317",  insecure=true
   121→//	"https://collector.example:4317" → host="collector.example:4317", insecure=false
   122→//	""                            → host=defaultEndpoint,  insecure=true
   123→func parseEndpoint(raw string) (host string, insecure bool) {
   124→	if raw == "" {
   125→		return defaultEndpoint, true
   126→	}
   127→
   128→	u, err := url.Parse(raw)
   129→	if err != nil || u.Host == "" {
   130→		// Not a URL — treat the whole string as host:port (bare address).
   131→		return raw, true
   132→	}
   133→
   134→	// Parsed successfully as a URL with a scheme.
   135→	host = u.Host
   136→	insecure = u.Scheme != "https"
   137→	return host, insecure
   138→}

   140→// Init configures the OTel tracing and metrics subsystem. Thread-safe and idempotent — only the
   141→// first call takes effect. When Enabled is false the global no-op provider remains
   142→// active, so callers can emit spans/events and record metrics safely with zero overhead.
   143→func Init(ctx context.Context, opts Options) error {
   144→	var initErr error
   145→	initOnce.Do(func() {
   146→		if !opts.Enabled {
   147→			telemetryLogger().Info("Telemetry disabled, using no-op provider")
   148→			return
   149→		}
   150→
   151→		// Route OTel SDK errors (export failures, connection issues) through slog
   152→		// so they appear in debug logs alongside our own telemetry messages.
   153→		otel.SetErrorHandler(otel.ErrorHandlerFunc(func(err error) {
   154→			telemetryLogger().Warn("OTel SDK error", "error", err)
   155→		}))
   156→
   157→		serviceName := opts.ServiceName
   158→		if serviceName == "" {
   159→			serviceName = "specstory-cli"
   160→		}
   161→
   162→		// Parse the endpoint to extract a bare host:port for WithEndpoint and
   163→		// determine TLS mode from the scheme. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is
   164→		// conventionally a full URL (e.g. "http://localhost:4317"), but
   165→		// WithEndpoint expects just "host:port".
   166→		host, insecure := parseEndpoint(opts.Endpoint)
   167→
   168→		// Create shared resource for both traces and metrics.
   169→		// Use resource.New() with detectors to pick up OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES env var.
   170→		res, err := resource.New(ctx,
   171→			resource.WithFromEnv(),      // OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and OTEL_SERVICE_NAME
   172→			resource.WithTelemetrySDK(), // telemetry.sdk.* attributes
   173→			resource.WithHost(),         // host.* attributes
   174→			resource.WithAttributes(attribute.String("service.name", serviceName)), // explicit service name (can override env)
   175→		)
   176→		if err != nil {
   177→			initErr = fmt.Errorf("create OTel resource: %w", err)
   178→			return
   179→		}
   180→
   181→		// Log the resource attributes for debugging
   182→		telemetryLogger().Debug("Resource attributes created",
   183→			"attributes", res.Attributes(),
   184→			"OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES", os.Getenv("OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES"),
   185→		)
   186→
   187→		// Initialize tracing
   188→		if err := initTracing(ctx, host, insecure, res); err != nil {
   189→			initErr = err
   190→			return
   191→		}
   192→
   193→		// Initialize metrics
   194→		if err := initMetrics(ctx, host, insecure, res); err != nil {
   195→			// Roll back tracing initialization to avoid half-initialized state
   196→			telemetryLogger().Warn("Metrics init failed, rolling back tracing", "error", err)
   197→			if traceProvider != nil {
   198→				if shutdownErr := traceProvider.Shutdown(ctx); shutdownErr != nil {
   199→					telemetryLogger().Warn("Failed to shutdown trace provider during rollback", "error", shutdownErr)
   200→				}
   201→				traceProvider = nil
   202→				// Use no-op provider instead of nil per OTel documentation
   203→				otel.SetTracerProvider(noop.NewTracerProvider())
   204→			}
   205→			initErr = err
   206→			return
   207→		}
   208→
   209→		metricsEnabled = true
   210→
   211→		// Parse OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and store as common metric attributes.
   212→		// This ensures resource attributes appear as metric tags in backends like Datadog
   213→		// that may not automatically promote resource-level attributes to metric tags.
   214→		commonMetricAttrs = parseResourceAttributes()
   215→		if len(commonMetricAttrs) > 0 {
   216→			telemetryLogger().Debug("Parsed OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES for metrics",
   217→				"count", len(commonMetricAttrs),
   218→				"attributes", commonMetricAttrs,
   219→			)
   220→		}
   221→
   222→		telemetryLogger().Info("Telemetry initialised",
   223→			"endpoint", host,
   224→			"insecure", insecure,
   225→			"serviceName", serviceName,
   226→		)
   227→	})
   228→
   229→	return initErr
   230→}

   232→// initTracing sets up the trace provider and exporter.
   233→func initTracing(ctx context.Context, host string, insecure bool, res *resource.Resource) error {
   234→	exporterOpts := []otlptracegrpc.Option{
   235→		otlptracegrpc.WithEndpoint(host),
   236→	}
   237→	if insecure {
   238→		exporterOpts = append(exporterOpts, otlptracegrpc.WithInsecure())
   239→	}
   240→
   241→	exporter, err := otlptracegrpc.New(ctx, exporterOpts...)
   242→	if err != nil {
   243→		return fmt.Errorf("create OTLP trace exporter: %w", err)
   244→	}
   245→
   246→	traceProvider = sdktrace.NewTracerProvider(
   247→		sdktrace.WithBatcher(exporter),
   248→		sdktrace.WithResource(res),
   249→	)
   250→	otel.SetTracerProvider(traceProvider)
   251→
   252→	return nil
   253→}

   418→// Shutdown flushes pending spans/metrics and shuts down both providers.
   419→// Safe to call even when Init was never called or telemetry is disabled.
   420→// For short-lived CLIs, this performs explicit ForceFlush calls before shutdown
   421→// to ensure all data is exported before the process exits.
   422→func Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error {
   423→	var errs []error
   424→
   425→	if traceProvider != nil {
   426→		telemetryLogger().Info("Flushing and shutting down trace provider")
   427→		// ForceFlush ensures all pending spans are exported before shutdown.
   428→		// This is critical for short-lived CLIs that may exit before the
   429→		// periodic exporter has time to run.
   430→		if err := traceProvider.ForceFlush(ctx); err != nil {
   431→			telemetryLogger().Warn("Failed to flush trace provider", "error", err)
   432→		}
   433→		if err := traceProvider.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
   434→			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("shutdown trace provider: %w", err))
   435→		}
   436→	}
   437→
   438→	if meterProvider != nil {
   439→		telemetryLogger().Info("Flushing and shutting down meter provider")
   440→		// ForceFlush ensures all pending metrics are exported before shutdown.
   441→		// The periodic reader has a 10-second interval, so without this,
   442→		// metrics from short CLI runs would never be sent.
   443→		if err := meterProvider.ForceFlush(ctx); err != nil {
   444→			telemetryLogger().Warn("Failed to flush meter provider", "error", err)
   445→		}
   446→		if err := meterProvider.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
   447→			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("shutdown meter provider: %w", err))
   448→		}
   449→	}
   450→
   451→	if len(errs) > 0 {
   452→		return errs[0] // Return first error
   453→	}
   454→	return nil
   455→}
   456→
   457→// ForceFlush explicitly flushes all pending spans and metrics.
   458→// Call this at the end of short-lived commands to ensure data is exported
   459→// before the command returns. Safe to call when telemetry is disabled.
   460→func ForceFlush(ctx context.Context) error {
   461→	var errs []error
   462→
   463→	if traceProvider != nil {
   464→		telemetryLogger().Debug("Force flushing trace provider")
   465→		if err := traceProvider.ForceFlush(ctx); err != nil {
   466→			telemetryLogger().Warn("Failed to force flush trace provider", "error", err)
   467→			errs = append(errs, err)
   468→		}
   469→	}
   470→
   471→	if meterProvider != nil {
   472→		telemetryLogger().Debug("Force flushing meter provider")
   473→		if err := meterProvider.ForceFlush(ctx); err != nil {
   474→			telemetryLogger().Warn("Failed to force flush meter provider", "error", err)
   475→			errs = append(errs, err)
   476→		}
   477→	}
   478→
   479→	if len(errs) > 0 {
   480→		return errs[0]
   481→	}
   482→	return nil
   483→}

   500→// ContextWithSessionTrace returns a context that will cause any spans started
   501→// from it to share the same trace ID (derived deterministically from sessionID).
   502→// This groups all spans for a given session into a single trace, even across
   503→// multiple invocations (e.g., in autosave mode where processSingleSession is
   504→// called repeatedly as the session file grows).
   505→func ContextWithSessionTrace(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) context.Context {
   506→	traceID := traceIDFromSessionID(sessionID)
   507→	spanID := spanIDFromSessionID(sessionID)
   508→
   509→	// Create a SpanContext with both deterministic trace ID and span ID.
   510→	// In OpenTelemetry-Go, a SpanContext is only valid if both TraceID and SpanID
   511→	// are valid. We mark it as Remote so child spans inherit the trace ID.
   512→	sc := trace.NewSpanContext(trace.SpanContextConfig{
   513→		TraceID:    traceID,
   514→		SpanID:     spanID,
   515→		TraceFlags: trace.FlagsSampled, // Ensure it's sampled
   516→		Remote:     true,               // Mark as remote parent
   517→	})
   518→
   519→	// Inject the SpanContext as a remote parent so child spans inherit the trace ID
   520→	return trace.ContextWithRemoteSpanContext(ctx, sc)
   521→}
   522→
   523→// traceIDFromSessionID generates a deterministic 16-byte trace ID from a session ID
   524→// by hashing the session ID with SHA-256 and taking the first 16 bytes.
   525→func traceIDFromSessionID(sessionID string) trace.TraceID {
   526→	hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(sessionID))
   527→	var traceID trace.TraceID
   528→	copy(traceID[:], hash[:16])
   529→	return traceID
   530→}
   531→
   532→// spanIDFromSessionID generates a deterministic 8-byte span ID from a session ID
   533→// by hashing the session ID with SHA-256 and taking bytes 16-24.
   534→// This ensures the span ID is different from the trace ID but still deterministic.
   535→func spanIDFromSessionID(sessionID string) trace.SpanID {
   536→	hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(sessionID))
   537→	var spanID trace.SpanID
   538→	copy(spanID[:], hash[16:24])
   539→	return spanID
   540→}

   549→	attrs = append(attrs, specific...)
   550→	attrs = append(attrs, commonMetricAttrs...)

   159→// ProcessExchangeSpans creates child spans for all exchanges in a session.
   160→// This is a helper that creates spans, sets attributes, and ends them immediately
   161→// since exchange processing is retrospective (data already exists).
   162→// When noPrompts is true, the prompt_text attribute will be empty for privacy.
   163→func ProcessExchangeSpans(ctx context.Context, stats SessionStats, exchanges []schema.Exchange, noPrompts bool) {
   164→	telemetryLogger().Debug("Creating exchange spans",
   165→		"sessionId", stats.SessionID,
   166→		"exchangeCount", len(exchanges),
   167→		"noPrompts", noPrompts,
   168→	)
   169→	for i, exchange := range exchanges {
   170→		_, exchangeSpan := startExchangeSpan(ctx, stats.SessionID, exchange.ExchangeID, i)
   171→		exchangeStats := computeExchangeStats(exchange, i)
   172→		if noPrompts {
   173→			exchangeStats.PromptText = ""
   174→		}
   175→		setExchangeSpanAttributes(exchangeSpan, exchangeStats)
   176→		exchangeSpan.End()
   177→	}
   178→}

   204→// --- Exchange Helpers ---
   205→
   206→// extractToolInfo extracts tool usage information from an exchange.
   207→// Returns: comma-separated unique tool names, comma-separated unique tool types, and total tool count.
   208→func extractToolInfo(exchange schema.Exchange) (toolNames string, toolTypes string, toolCount int) {
   209→	nameSet := make(map[string]bool)
   210→	typeSet := make(map[string]bool)
   211→
   212→	for _, msg := range exchange.Messages {
   213→		if msg.Tool != nil && msg.Tool.Name != "" {
   214→			toolCount++
   215→			nameSet[msg.Tool.Name] = true
   216→			if msg.Tool.Type != "" {
   217→				typeSet[msg.Tool.Type] = true
   218→			}
   219→		}
   220→	}
   221→
   222→	// Build unique tool names list (sorted for deterministic output)
   223→	var names []string
   224→	for n := range nameSet {
   225→		names = append(names, n)
   226→	}
   227→	sort.Strings(names)
   228→
   229→	// Build unique tool types list (sorted for deterministic output)
   230→	var types []string
   231→	for t := range typeSet {
   232→		types = append(types, t)
   233→	}
   234→	sort.Strings(types)
   235→
   236→	return strings.Join(names, ","), strings.Join(types, ","), toolCount
   237→}
   238→
   239→// extractUserPromptText finds the first user message in an exchange and returns its text content.
   240→func extractUserPromptText(exchange schema.Exchange) string {
   241→	for _, msg := range exchange.Messages {
   242→		if msg.Role == schema.RoleUser {
   243→			// Concatenate all text content parts
   244→			var text string
   245→			for _, part := range msg.Content {
   246→				if part.Type == schema.ContentTypeText {
   247→					if text != "" {
   248→						text += "\n"
   249→					}
   250→					text += part.Text
   251→				}
   252→			}
   253→			return text
   254→		}
   255→	}
   256→	return ""
   257→}
   258→
   259→// extractModel finds the model used in an exchange by looking at agent messages.
   260→// Returns the model from the first agent message that has one set.
   261→func extractModel(exchange schema.Exchange) string {
   262→	for _, msg := range exchange.Messages {
   263→		if msg.Role == schema.RoleAgent && msg.Model != "" {
   264→			return msg.Model
   265→		}
   266→	}
   267→	return ""
   268→}
   269→
   270→// --- Counting Helpers ---
   271→
   272→// countSessionMessages counts total messages across all exchanges.
   273→func countSessionMessages(exchanges []schema.Exchange) int {
   274→	count := 0
   275→	for _, exchange := range exchanges {
   276→		count += len(exchange.Messages)
   277→	}
   278→	return count
   279→}
   280→
   281→// countSessionTools counts total tools and unique tool types across all exchanges.
   282→// Returns: total tool count, unique tool type count.
   283→func countSessionTools(exchanges []schema.Exchange) (toolCount int, toolTypeCount int) {
   284→	typeSet := make(map[string]bool)
   285→
   286→	for _, exchange := range exchanges {
   287→		for _, msg := range exchange.Messages {
   288→			if msg.Tool != nil && msg.Tool.Name != "" {
   289→				toolCount++
   290→				if msg.Tool.Type != "" {
   291→					typeSet[msg.Tool.Type] = true
   292→				}
   293→			}
   294→		}
   295→	}
   296→
   297→	return toolCount, len(typeSet)
   298→}
   299→
   300→// countExchangeTokens aggregates token usage for a single exchange.
   301→// Handles Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and Droid CLI specific token fields.
   302→func countExchangeTokens(exchange schema.Exchange) TokenUsage {
   303→	var usage TokenUsage
   304→	for _, msg := range exchange.Messages {
   305→		if msg.Usage != nil {
   306→			// Common fields (all providers)
   307→			usage.InputTokens += msg.Usage.InputTokens
   308→			usage.OutputTokens += msg.Usage.OutputTokens
   309→			// Claude Code specific (also used by Droid CLI)
   310→			usage.CacheCreationInputTokens += msg.Usage.CacheCreationInputTokens
   311→			usage.CacheReadInputTokens += msg.Usage.CacheReadInputTokens
   312→			// Codex CLI specific
   313→			usage.CachedInputTokens += msg.Usage.CachedInputTokens
   314→			usage.ReasoningOutputTokens += msg.Usage.ReasoningOutputTokens
   315→			// Gemini CLI specific
   316→			usage.CachedTokens += msg.Usage.CachedTokens
   317→			usage.ThoughtTokens += msg.Usage.ThoughtTokens
   318→			usage.ToolTokens += msg.Usage.ToolTokens
   319→			// Droid CLI specific
   320→			usage.ThinkingTokens += msg.Usage.ThinkingTokens
   321→		}
   322→	}
   323→	return usage
   324→}
   325→
   326→// countSessionTokens aggregates token usage across all exchanges in a session.
   327→// Handles Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and Droid CLI specific token fields.
   328→func countSessionTokens(exchanges []schema.Exchange) TokenUsage {
   329→	var total TokenUsage
   330→	for _, exchange := range exchanges {
   331→		exchangeUsage := countExchangeTokens(exchange)
   332→		// Common fields (all providers)
   333→		total.InputTokens += exchangeUsage.InputTokens
   334→		total.OutputTokens += exchangeUsage.OutputTokens
   335→		// Claude Code specific (also used by Droid CLI)
   336→		total.CacheCreationInputTokens += exchangeUsage.CacheCreationInputTokens
   337→		total.CacheReadInputTokens += exchangeUsage.CacheReadInputTokens
   338→		// Codex CLI specific
   339→		total.CachedInputTokens += exchangeUsage.CachedInputTokens
   340→		total.ReasoningOutputTokens += exchangeUsage.ReasoningOutputTokens
   341→		// Gemini CLI specific
   342→		total.CachedTokens += exchangeUsage.CachedTokens
   343→		total.ThoughtTokens += exchangeUsage.ThoughtTokens
   344→		total.ToolTokens += exchangeUsage.ToolTokens
   345→		// Droid CLI specific
   346→		total.ThinkingTokens += exchangeUsage.ThinkingTokens
   347→	}

     8→)

    10→// --- extractToolInfo tests ---
    11→
    12→func TestExtractToolInfo(t *testing.T) {
    13→	tests := []struct {
    14→		name          string
    15→		exchange      schema.Exchange
    16→		wantToolNames string
    17→		wantToolTypes string
    18→		wantToolCount int
    19→	}{
    20→		{
    21→			name:          "empty exchange",
    22→			exchange:      schema.Exchange{},
    23→			wantToolNames: "",
    24→			wantToolTypes: "",
    25→			wantToolCount: 0,
    26→		},
    27→		{
    28→			name: "no tools in messages",
    29→			exchange: schema.Exchange{
    30→				Messages: []schema.Message{
    31→					{Role: schema.RoleUser, Content: []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "hello"}}},
    32→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Content: []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "hi"}}},
    33→				},
    34→			},
    35→			wantToolNames: "",
    36→			wantToolTypes: "",
    37→			wantToolCount: 0,
    38→		},
    39→		{
    40→			name: "single tool",
    41→			exchange: schema.Exchange{
    42→				Messages: []schema.Message{
    43→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "Read", Type: "read"}},
    44→				},
    45→			},
    46→			wantToolNames: "Read",
    47→			wantToolTypes: "read",
    48→			wantToolCount: 1,
    49→		},
    50→		{
    51→			name: "multiple different tools",
    52→			exchange: schema.Exchange{
    53→				Messages: []schema.Message{
    54→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "Read", Type: "read"}},
    55→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "Write", Type: "write"}},
    56→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "Bash", Type: "shell"}},
    57→				},
    58→			},
    59→			wantToolNames: "Bash,Read,Write",  // sorted alphabetically
    60→			wantToolTypes: "read,shell,write", // sorted alphabetically
    61→			wantToolCount: 3,
    62→		},
    63→		{
    64→			name: "duplicate tool names counted separately but listed once",
    65→			exchange: schema.Exchange{
    66→				Messages: []schema.Message{
    67→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "Read", Type: "read"}},
    68→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "Read", Type: "read"}},
    69→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "Write", Type: "write"}},
    70→				},
    71→			},
    72→			wantToolNames: "Read,Write",
    73→			wantToolTypes: "read,write",
    74→			wantToolCount: 3, // total count includes duplicates
    75→		},
    76→		{
    77→			name: "tool with empty type",
    78→			exchange: schema.Exchange{
    79→				Messages: []schema.Message{
    80→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "CustomTool", Type: ""}},
    81→				},
    82→			},
    83→			wantToolNames: "CustomTool",
    84→			wantToolTypes: "",
    85→			wantToolCount: 1,
    86→		},
    87→		{
    88→			name: "tool with nil Tool pointer ignored",
    89→			exchange: schema.Exchange{
    90→				Messages: []schema.Message{
    91→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: nil},
    92→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "Read", Type: "read"}},
    93→				},
    94→			},
    95→			wantToolNames: "Read",
    96→			wantToolTypes: "read",
    97→			wantToolCount: 1,
    98→		},
    99→		{
   100→			name: "tool with empty name ignored",
   101→			exchange: schema.Exchange{
   102→				Messages: []schema.Message{
   103→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "", Type: "read"}},
   104→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "Write", Type: "write"}},
   105→				},
   106→			},
   107→			wantToolNames: "Write",
   108→			wantToolTypes: "write",
   109→			wantToolCount: 1,
   110→		},
   111→	}
   112→
   113→	for _, tt := range tests {
   114→		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
   115→			gotNames, gotTypes, gotCount := extractToolInfo(tt.exchange)
   116→			if gotNames != tt.wantToolNames {
   117→				t.Errorf("extractToolInfo() toolNames = %q, want %q", gotNames, tt.wantToolNames)
   118→			}
   119→			if gotTypes != tt.wantToolTypes {
   120→				t.Errorf("extractToolInfo() toolTypes = %q, want %q", gotTypes, tt.wantToolTypes)
   121→			}
   122→			if gotCount != tt.wantToolCount {
   123→				t.Errorf("extractToolInfo() toolCount = %d, want %d", gotCount, tt.wantToolCount)
   124→			}
   125→		})
   126→	}
   127→}

   129→// --- extractUserPromptText tests ---
   130→
   131→func TestExtractUserPromptText(t *testing.T) {
   132→	tests := []struct {
   133→		name     string
   134→		exchange schema.Exchange
   135→		want     string
   136→	}{
   137→		{
   138→			name:     "empty exchange",

   141→		},
   142→		{
   143→			name: "no user message",
   144→			exchange: schema.Exchange{
   145→				Messages: []schema.Message{
   146→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Content: []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "response"}}},
   147→				},
   148→			},
   149→			want: "",
   150→		},
   151→		{
   152→			name: "single user message with text",
   153→			exchange: schema.Exchange{

   157→			},
   158→			want: "hello world",
   159→		},
   160→		{
   161→			name: "user message with multiple text parts",
   162→			exchange: schema.Exchange{
   163→				Messages: []schema.Message{
   164→					{Role: schema.RoleUser, Content: []schema.ContentPart{
   165→						{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "first part"},
   166→						{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "second part"},
   167→					}},
   168→				},
   169→			},
   170→			want: "first part\nsecond part",
   171→		},
   172→		{
   173→			name: "user message with mixed content types",
   174→			exchange: schema.Exchange{
   175→				Messages: []schema.Message{
   176→					{Role: schema.RoleUser, Content: []schema.ContentPart{
   177→						{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "text content"},
   178→						{Type: "image", Text: "should be ignored"},
   179→						{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "more text"},
   180→					}},
   181→				},
   182→			},
   183→			want: "text content\nmore text",
   184→		},
   185→		{
   186→			name: "first user message is used",

   188→				Messages: []schema.Message{
   189→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Content: []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "agent first"}}},
   190→					{Role: schema.RoleUser, Content: []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "user prompt"}}},
   191→					{Role: schema.RoleUser, Content: []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "second user message ignored"}}},
   192→				},
   193→			},
   194→			want: "user prompt",
   195→		},
   196→		{
   197→			name: "user message with empty content",
   198→			exchange: schema.Exchange{
   199→				Messages: []schema.Message{
   200→					{Role: schema.RoleUser, Content: []schema.ContentPart{}},
   201→				},
   202→			},
   203→			want: "",
   204→		},
   205→	}
   206→
   207→	for _, tt := range tests {
   208→		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
   209→			got := extractUserPromptText(tt.exchange)
   210→			if got != tt.want {
   211→				t.Errorf("extractUserPromptText() = %q, want %q", got, tt.want)
   212→			}
   213→		})
   214→	}
   215→}

   281→// --- countSessionTools tests ---
   282→
   283→func TestCountSessionTools(t *testing.T) {
   284→	tests := []struct {
   285→		name              string
   286→		exchanges         []schema.Exchange
   287→		wantToolCount     int
   288→		wantToolTypeCount int
   289→	}{
   290→		{
   291→			name:              "empty exchanges",
   292→			exchanges:         []schema.Exchange{},
   293→			wantToolCount:     0,
   294→			wantToolTypeCount: 0,
   295→		},
   296→		{
   297→			name: "no tools",
   298→			exchanges: []schema.Exchange{
   299→				{Messages: []schema.Message{{Role: schema.RoleUser}, {Role: schema.RoleAgent}}},
   300→			},
   301→			wantToolCount:     0,
   302→			wantToolTypeCount: 0,
   303→		},
   304→		{
   305→			name: "single tool",
   306→			exchanges: []schema.Exchange{
   307→				{Messages: []schema.Message{
   308→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "Read", Type: "read"}},
   309→				}},
   310→			},
   311→			wantToolCount:     1,
   312→			wantToolTypeCount: 1,
   313→		},
   314→		{
   315→			name: "tools across multiple exchanges",
   316→			exchanges: []schema.Exchange{
   317→				{Messages: []schema.Message{
   318→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "Read", Type: "read"}},
   319→				}},
   320→				{Messages: []schema.Message{
   321→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "Write", Type: "write"}},
   322→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "Bash", Type: "shell"}},
   323→				}},
   324→			},
   325→			wantToolCount:     3,
   326→			wantToolTypeCount: 3,
   327→		},
   328→		{
   329→			name: "duplicate tool types counted once",
   330→			exchanges: []schema.Exchange{
   331→				{Messages: []schema.Message{
   332→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "Read", Type: "read"}},
   333→					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "Glob", Type: "read"}},
   334→				}},
   335→			},
   336→			wantToolCount:     2,
   337→			wantToolTypeCount: 1, // both are "read" type
   338→		},
   339→	}
   340→
   341→	for _, tt := range tests {
   342→		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
   343→			gotCount, gotTypeCount := countSessionTools(tt.exchanges)
   344→			if gotCount != tt.wantToolCount {
   345→				t.Errorf("countSessionTools() toolCount = %d, want %d", gotCount, tt.wantToolCount)
   346→			}
   347→			if gotTypeCount != tt.wantToolTypeCount {
   348→				t.Errorf("countSessionTools() toolTypeCount = %d, want %d", gotTypeCount, tt.wantToolTypeCount)
   349→			}
   350→		})
   351→	}
   352→}

   600→// --- computeExchangeStats tests ---

   605→		exchange schema.Exchange

   229→// Load reads configuration from files and CLI flags.
   230→// Priority: CLI flags > local project config > user-level config
   231→// Note: For telemetry, OTEL_* env vars take highest priority per OTel conventions.
   232→//
   233→// Returns an error if a config file exists but cannot be parsed (TOML syntax error)
   234→// or cannot be read (permission denied, I/O error). Missing config files are not
   235→// treated as errors - they are simply skipped.
   236→func Load(cliOverrides *CLIOverrides) (*Config, error) {
   237→	cfg := &Config{}
   238→
   239→	// Load user-level config first (lowest priority)
   240→	userConfigPath := getUserConfigPath()
   241→	if userConfigPath != "" {
   242→		if err := loadTOMLFile(userConfigPath, cfg); err != nil {
   243→			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   244→				slog.Debug("No user-level config file found", "path", userConfigPath)
   245→				ensureDefaultUserConfig(userConfigPath)
   246→			} else {
   247→				// Parse error or permission denied - return error to caller
   248→				return cfg, fmt.Errorf("failed to load user config %s: %w", userConfigPath, err)
   249→			}
   250→		} else {
   251→			slog.Debug("Loaded user-level config", "path", userConfigPath)
   252→		}
   253→	}
   254→
   255→	// Load local project config (overwrites user-level)
   256→	localConfigPath := getLocalConfigPath()
   257→	if localConfigPath != "" {
   258→		if err := loadTOMLFile(localConfigPath, cfg); err != nil {
   259→			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   260→				slog.Debug("No local project config file found", "path", localConfigPath)
   261→			} else {
   262→				// Parse error or permission denied - return error to caller
   263→				return cfg, fmt.Errorf("failed to load project config %s: %w", localConfigPath, err)
   264→			}
   265→		} else {
   266→			slog.Debug("Loaded local project config", "path", localConfigPath)
   267→		}
   268→	}
   269→
   270→	// Apply CLI flag overrides (highest priority for most settings)
   271→	if cliOverrides != nil {
   272→		applyCLIOverrides(cfg, cliOverrides)
   273→	}
   274→
   275→	// Apply OTel environment variables (highest priority for telemetry only)
   276→	applyTelemetryEnvOverrides(cfg)
   277→
   278→	return cfg, nil
   279→}

   281→// GetUserConfigPath returns the path to ~/.specstory/cli/config.toml
   282→func GetUserConfigPath() string {
   283→	return getUserConfigPath()
   284→}
   285→
   286→// GetLocalConfigPath returns the path to .specstory/cli/config.toml in the current directory
   287→func GetLocalConfigPath() string {
   288→	return getLocalConfigPath()
   289→}
   290→
   291→// getUserConfigPath returns the path to ~/.specstory/cli/config.toml
   292→func getUserConfigPath() string {
   293→	home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
   294→	if err != nil {
   295→		slog.Debug("Could not determine home directory", "error", err)
   296→		return ""
   297→	}
   298→	return filepath.Join(home, SpecStoryDir, CLIDir, ConfigFileName)
   299→}
   300→
   301→// getLocalConfigPath returns the path to .specstory/cli/config.toml in the current directory
   302→func getLocalConfigPath() string {
   303→	cwd, err := os.Getwd()
   304→	if err != nil {
   305→		slog.Debug("Could not determine current directory", "error", err)
   306→		return ""
   307→	}
   308→	return filepath.Join(cwd, SpecStoryDir, CLIDir, ConfigFileName)
   309→}

   311→// processTemplate processes the default config template for a given level
   312→// ("user" or "project"). Template markers {u ...} and {p ...} delimit content
   313→// specific to user-level or project-level config files respectively.
   314→//
   315→// For level "user": content inside {u ...} is kept (markers stripped),
   316→// content inside {p ...} is removed entirely.
   317→// For level "project": the opposite applies.
   318→//
   319→// Markers can span multiple lines. The opening marker ({u or {p) appears at
   320→// the start of a line (after optional whitespace/comment prefix), and the
   321→// closing } appears at the end of a line.
   322→func processTemplate(template, level string) string {
   323→	var result strings.Builder
   324→	keepTag := "{u"
   325→	stripTag := "{p"
   326→	if level == "project" {
   327→		keepTag = "{p"
   328→		stripTag = "{u"
   329→	}
   330→
   331→	insideKeep := false
   332→	insideStrip := false
   333→
   334→	for line := range strings.SplitSeq(template, "\n") {
   335→		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
   336→		// Remove any leading "# " to inspect the marker
   337→		bare := strings.TrimPrefix(trimmed, "# ")
   338→
   339→		switch {
   340→		case insideStrip:
   341→			// Check for closing brace — ends the stripped block
   342→			if strings.HasSuffix(bare, "}") {
   343→				insideStrip = false
   344→			}
   345→			// Drop the entire line regardless
   346→			continue
   347→
   348→		case insideKeep:
   349→			// Check for closing brace — ends the kept block
   350→			if strings.HasSuffix(bare, "}") {
   351→				insideKeep = false
   352→				// Strip the trailing } from the line
   353→				idx := strings.LastIndex(line, "}")
   354→				line = line[:idx]
   355→				// Only emit if something remains after stripping
   356→				if strings.TrimSpace(line) == "" || strings.TrimSpace(line) == "#" {
   357→					continue
   358→				}
   359→			}
   360→			result.WriteString(line)
   361→			result.WriteString("\n")
   362→
   363→		case strings.HasPrefix(bare, keepTag+" "):
   364→			insideKeep = true
   365→			// prefix is everything before the bare marker (e.g. "# ")
   366→			prefix := line[:strings.Index(line, bare)]
   367→			// Check if single-line block (closing } on same line)
   368→			if strings.HasSuffix(bare, "}") {
   369→				insideKeep = false
   370→				// Extract content between tag and closing brace
   371→				content := strings.TrimSpace(bare[len(keepTag)+1 : len(bare)-1])
   372→				reconstructed := prefix + content
   373→				if strings.TrimSpace(reconstructed) == "" || strings.TrimSpace(reconstructed) == "#" {
   374→					continue
   375→				}
   376→				result.WriteString(reconstructed)
   377→				result.WriteString("\n")
   378→			} else {
   379→				// Multi-line: strip the marker prefix, keep content after it
   380→				content := strings.TrimSpace(bare[len(keepTag)+1:])
   381→				reconstructed := prefix + content
   382→				if strings.TrimSpace(reconstructed) == "" || strings.TrimSpace(reconstructed) == "#" {
   383→					continue
   384→				}
   385→				result.WriteString(reconstructed)
   386→				result.WriteString("\n")
   387→			}
   388→
   389→		case strings.HasPrefix(bare, stripTag+" "):
   390→			insideStrip = true
   391→			// Check if single-line block (closing } on same line)
   392→			if strings.HasSuffix(bare, "}") {
   393→				insideStrip = false
   394→			}
   395→			continue
   396→
   397→		default:
   398→			result.WriteString(line)
   399→			result.WriteString("\n")
   400→		}
   401→	}
   402→
   403→	// Remove trailing extra newline that accumulates from the split
   404→	out := result.String()
   405→	if strings.HasSuffix(out, "\n\n") && !strings.HasSuffix(template, "\n\n") {
   406→		out = out[:len(out)-1]
   407→	}
   408→	return out
   409→}

   411→// ensureDefaultUserConfig creates a default user-level config file with all
   412→// options commented out. This makes the config discoverable without changing
   413→// any behavior. Failures are silently ignored — this is a convenience, not
   414→// a requirement.
   415→func ensureDefaultUserConfig(path string) {
   416→	dir := filepath.Dir(path)
   417→	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0755); err != nil {
   418→		slog.Debug("Could not create config directory", "path", dir, "error", err)
   419→		return
   420→	}
   421→	processed := processTemplate(defaultConfigTemplate, "user")
   422→	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(processed), 0644); err != nil {
   423→		slog.Debug("Could not write default config file", "path", path, "error", err)
   424→		return
   425→	}
   426→	slog.Debug("Created default user config file", "path", path)
   427→}
   428→
   429→// EnsureDefaultProjectConfig creates a default project-level config file at
   430→// .specstory/cli/config.toml if one doesn't already exist. All options are
   431→// commented out so the file is self-documenting but inert.
   432→//
   433→// This should only be called from commands that imply active project work
   434→// (run, sync, watch) to avoid scattering config files in arbitrary directories.
   435→// Failures are silently ignored — this is a convenience, not a requirement.
   436→func EnsureDefaultProjectConfig() {
   437→	path := getLocalConfigPath()
   438→	if path == "" {
   439→		return
   440→	}
   441→	// Don't overwrite an existing file
   442→	if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
   443→		return
   444→	}
   445→	dir := filepath.Dir(path)
   446→	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0755); err != nil {
   447→		slog.Debug("Could not create config directory", "path", dir, "error", err)
   448→		return
   449→	}
   450→	processed := processTemplate(defaultConfigTemplate, "project")
   451→	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(processed), 0644); err != nil {
   452→		slog.Debug("Could not write default config file", "path", path, "error", err)
   453→		return
   454→	}
   455→	slog.Debug("Created default project config file", "path", path)
   456→}

   481→// ConfigValidationResult holds the result of validating a config file.
   482→type ConfigValidationResult struct {
   483→	Path        string   // Path to the config file
   484→	Exists      bool     // Whether the file exists
   485→	ValidTOML   bool     // Whether the file is valid TOML
   486→	ParseError  string   // TOML parse error message, if any
   487→	UnknownKeys []string // Keys in the file that don't map to any known config field
   488→}
   489→
   490→// ValidateConfigFile checks a config file for validity and schema conformance.
   491→// Returns a result indicating whether the file exists, is valid TOML, and
   492→// whether it contains any unknown sections or properties.
   493→func ValidateConfigFile(path string) ConfigValidationResult {
   494→	result := ConfigValidationResult{Path: path}
   495→
   496→	// Check if file exists
   497→	if _, err := os.Stat(path); os.IsNotExist(err) {
   498→		return result
   499→	}
   500→	result.Exists = true
   501→
   502→	// Try to decode and check for unknown keys
   503→	var cfg Config
   504→	md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
   505→	if err != nil {
   506→		result.ParseError = err.Error()
   507→		return result
   508→	}
   509→	result.ValidTOML = true
   510→
   511→	// Check for keys in the TOML that didn't map to any struct field.
   512→	// Filter out child keys when the parent section is already unknown
   513→	// (e.g., if [bogus] is unknown, don't also report bogus.foo).
   514→	undecoded := md.Undecoded()
   515→	unknownSections := make(map[string]bool)
   516→	for _, key := range undecoded {
   517→		if len(key) == 1 {
   518→			unknownSections[key[0]] = true
   519→		}
   520→	}
   521→	for _, key := range undecoded {
   522→		// Skip child keys whose parent section is already flagged
   523→		if len(key) > 1 && unknownSections[key[0]] {
   524→			continue
   525→		}
   526→		result.UnknownKeys = append(result.UnknownKeys, key.String())
   527→	}
   528→
   529→	return result
   530→}

   532→// applyCLIOverrides applies CLI flag overrides to the config.
   533→func applyCLIOverrides(cfg *Config, o *CLIOverrides) {
   534→	// Local sync

   545→
   546→	// Version check (--no-version-check sets enabled to false)

   552→	// Cloud sync (--no-cloud-sync sets enabled to false)

   555→		cfg.CloudSync.Enabled = &disabled
   556→	}
   557→
   558→	// Local sync (--only-cloud-sync sets enabled to false)

   561→		cfg.LocalSync.Enabled = &disabled
   562→	}
   563→
   564→	// Logging flags only override if explicitly set (true)
   565→	if o.Console {

   567→		cfg.Logging.Console = &enabled
   568→	}
   569→	if o.Log {
   570→		enabled := true
   571→		cfg.Logging.Log = &enabled
   572→	}
   573→	if o.Debug {
   574→		enabled := true
   575→		cfg.Logging.Debug = &enabled
   576→	}
   577→	if o.Silent {
   578→		enabled := true
   579→		cfg.Logging.Silent = &enabled
   580→	}
   581→
   582→	// Analytics (--no-usage-analytics sets enabled to false)
   583→	if o.NoAnalytics {

    45→// FormatFilenameTimestamp formats a timestamp for use in filenames.
    46→// The format is filesystem-safe and matches the markdown title format.
    47→func FormatFilenameTimestamp(t time.Time, useUTC bool) string {
    48→	if useUTC {
    49→		// Use UTC with Z suffix: "2006-01-02_15-04-05Z"
    50→		return t.UTC().Format("2006-01-02_15-04-05") + "Z"
    51→	}
    52→	// Use local timezone with offset: "2006-01-02_15-04-05-0700"
    53→	return t.Local().Format("2006-01-02_15-04-05-0700")
    54→}

   145→	// Write file if needed (skip if only-cloud-sync is enabled)
   146→	if !onlyCloudSync {
   147→		if !identicalContent {
   148→			// Ensure history directory exists (handles deletion during long-running watch/run)
   149→			if err := utils.EnsureHistoryDirectoryExists(config); err != nil {
   150→				return 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to ensure history directory: %w", err)
   151→			}
   152→			err := os.WriteFile(fileFullPath, []byte(markdownContent), 0644)
   153→			if err != nil {
   154→				// Track write error
   155→				if isAutosave {
   156→					analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventAutosaveError, analytics.Properties{
   157→						"session_id":      session.SessionID,
   158→						"error":           err.Error(),
   159→						"only_cloud_sync": onlyCloudSync,
   160→					})
   161→				} else {
   162→					analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventSyncMarkdownError, analytics.Properties{
   163→						"session_id":      session.SessionID,
   164→						"error":           err.Error(),
   165→						"only_cloud_sync": onlyCloudSync,
   166→					})
   167→				}
   168→				return 0, fmt.Errorf("error writing markdown file: %w", err)
   169→			}
   170→
   171→			// Track successful write
   172→			if isAutosave {
   173→				if !fileExists {
   174→					// New file created during autosave
   175→					analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventAutosaveNew, analytics.Properties{
   176→						"session_id":      session.SessionID,
   177→						"only_cloud_sync": onlyCloudSync,
   178→					})
   179→				} else {
   180→					// File updated during autosave
   181→					analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventAutosaveSuccess, analytics.Properties{
   182→						"session_id":      session.SessionID,
   183→						"only_cloud_sync": onlyCloudSync,
   184→					})
   185→				}
   186→			} else {
   187→				if !fileExists {
   188→					// New file created during manual sync
   189→					analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventSyncMarkdownNew, analytics.Properties{
   190→						"session_id":      session.SessionID,
   191→						"only_cloud_sync": onlyCloudSync,
   192→					})
   193→				} else {
   194→					// File updated during manual sync
   195→					analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventSyncMarkdownSuccess, analytics.Properties{
   196→						"session_id":      session.SessionID,
   197→						"only_cloud_sync": onlyCloudSync,
   198→					})
   199→				}
   200→			}
   201→
   202→			slog.Info("Successfully wrote file",
   203→				"sessionId", session.SessionID,
   204→				"path", fileFullPath)
   205→		}
   206→
   207→		// Determine outcome for user feedback
   208→		if identicalContent {
   209→			outcome = "up to date (skipped)"
   210→		} else if fileExists {
   211→			outcome = "updated"
   212→		} else {
   213→			outcome = "created"
   214→		}
   215→	} else {
   216→		// Only cloud sync mode - no local file operations
   217→		outcome = "synced to cloud only"
   218→		slog.Info("Skipping local file write (only-cloud-sync mode)",
   219→			"sessionId", session.SessionID)
   220→	}
   221→
   222→	// Trigger cloud sync with provider-specific data
   223→	// In only-cloud-sync mode: always sync (no file to check for identical content)
   224→	// In normal mode: skip sync only if identical content AND in autosave mode
   225→	if onlyCloudSync || !identicalContent || !isAutosave {
   226→		cloud.SyncSessionToCloud(session.SessionID, fileFullPath, markdownContent, []byte(session.RawData), session.SessionData.Provider.Name, isAutosave)
   227→	}
   228→
   229→	if showOutput && !log.IsSilent() {
   230→		fmt.Printf(" %s\n", outcome)
   231→		fmt.Println() // Visual separation
   232→	}
   233→
   234→	return markdownSize, nil
   235→}

   107→// GetIntFromMap safely extracts an int from a map[string]interface{}.
   108→// JSON numbers are unmarshaled as float64, so we handle that case.
   109→func GetIntFromMap(m map[string]interface{}, key string) int {
   110→	if m == nil {
   111→		return 0
   112→	}
   113→	if val, ok := m[key]; ok {
   114→		switch v := val.(type) {
   115→		case float64:
   116→			return int(v)
   117→		case int64:
   118→			return int(v)
   119→		case int:
   120→			return v
   121→		}
   122→	}
   123→	return 0
   124→}

   147→// Validate checks the SessionData against schema constraints and logs warnings for any issues.
   148→// Returns true if validation passed, false if there were any issues.
   149→func (s *SessionData) Validate() bool {
   150→	valid := true
   151→
   152→	// Check schema version
   153→	if s.SchemaVersion != "1.0" {
   154→		slog.Warn("schema validation: schemaVersion must be '1.0'", "got", s.SchemaVersion)
   155→		valid = false
   156→	}
   157→
   158→	// Check required root fields
   159→	if s.Provider.ID == "" {
   160→		slog.Warn("schema validation: provider.id is required")
   161→		valid = false
   162→	}
   163→	if s.Provider.Name == "" {
   164→		slog.Warn("schema validation: provider.name is required")
   165→		valid = false
   166→	}
   167→	if s.Provider.Version == "" {
   168→		slog.Warn("schema validation: provider.version is required")
   169→		valid = false
   170→	}
   171→	if s.SessionID == "" {
   172→		slog.Warn("schema validation: sessionId is required")
   173→		valid = false
   174→	}
   175→	if s.CreatedAt == "" {
   176→		slog.Warn("schema validation: createdAt is required")
   177→		valid = false
   178→	}
   179→	if s.WorkspaceRoot == "" {
   180→		slog.Warn("schema validation: workspaceRoot is required")
   181→		valid = false
   182→	}
   183→
   184→	// Validate each exchange
   185→	for i, exchange := range s.Exchanges {
   186→		if exchange.ExchangeID == "" {
   187→			slog.Warn("schema validation: exchange.exchangeId is required", "exchangeIndex", i)
   188→			valid = false
   189→		}
   190→
   191→		// Validate each message in the exchange
   192→		for j, msg := range exchange.Messages {
   193→			if !msg.validate(i, j) {
   194→				valid = false
   195→			}
   196→		}
   197→	}
   198→
   199→	return valid
   200→}
   201→
   202→// validate checks a single message against schema constraints.
   203→func (m *Message) validate(exchangeIndex, messageIndex int) bool {
   204→	valid := true
   205→	logCtx := []any{"exchangeIndex", exchangeIndex, "messageIndex", messageIndex}
   206→
   207→	// Check role is valid
   208→	if m.Role != RoleUser && m.Role != RoleAgent {
   209→		slog.Warn("schema validation: message.role must be 'user' or 'agent'",
   210→			append(logCtx, "got", m.Role)...)
   211→		valid = false
   212→	}
   213→
   214→	// User message constraints
   215→	if m.Role == RoleUser {
   216→		if len(m.Content) == 0 {
   217→			slog.Warn("schema validation: user message must have non-empty content", logCtx...)
   218→			valid = false
   219→		}
   220→		if m.Tool != nil {
   221→			slog.Warn("schema validation: user message cannot have tool", logCtx...)
   222→			valid = false
   223→		}
   224→		if m.Model != "" {
   225→			slog.Warn("schema validation: user message cannot have model", logCtx...)
   226→			valid = false
   227→		}
   228→	}
   229→
   230→	// Agent message constraints: must have at least one of content, tool, or pathHints
   231→	if m.Role == RoleAgent {
   232→		hasContent := len(m.Content) > 0
   233→		hasTool := m.Tool != nil
   234→		hasPathHints := len(m.PathHints) > 0
   235→		if !hasContent && !hasTool && !hasPathHints {
   236→			slog.Warn("schema validation: agent message must have content, tool, or pathHints", logCtx...)
   237→			valid = false
   238→		}
   239→	}
   240→
   241→	// Validate content parts
   242→	for k, part := range m.Content {
   243→		if !part.validate(exchangeIndex, messageIndex, k) {
   244→			valid = false
   245→		}
   246→	}
   247→
   248→	// Validate tool if present
   249→	if m.Tool != nil {
   250→		if !m.Tool.validate(exchangeIndex, messageIndex) {
   251→			valid = false
   252→		}
   253→	}
   254→
   255→	return valid
   256→}
   257→
   258→// validate checks a single content part against schema constraints.
   259→func (c *ContentPart) validate(exchangeIndex, messageIndex, partIndex int) bool {
   260→	valid := true
   261→	logCtx := []any{"exchangeIndex", exchangeIndex, "messageIndex", messageIndex, "partIndex", partIndex}
   262→
   263→	if c.Type != ContentTypeText && c.Type != ContentTypeThinking {
   264→		slog.Warn("schema validation: contentPart.type must be 'text' or 'thinking'",
   265→			append(logCtx, "got", c.Type)...)
   266→		valid = false
   267→	}
   268→
   269→	return valid
   270→}
   271→
   272→// validate checks tool info against schema constraints.
   273→func (t *ToolInfo) validate(exchangeIndex, messageIndex int) bool {
   274→	valid := true
   275→	logCtx := []any{"exchangeIndex", exchangeIndex, "messageIndex", messageIndex}
   276→
   277→	if t.Name == "" {
   278→		slog.Warn("schema validation: tool.name is required", logCtx...)
   279→		valid = false
   280→	}
   281→
   282→	validTypes := map[string]bool{
   283→		ToolTypeWrite:   true,
   284→		ToolTypeRead:    true,
   285→		ToolTypeSearch:  true,
   286→		ToolTypeShell:   true,
   287→		ToolTypeTask:    true,
   288→		ToolTypeGeneric: true,
   289→		ToolTypeUnknown: true,

   291→	if !validTypes[t.Type] {

   293→			append(logCtx, "got", t.Type)...)
   294→		valid = false
   295→	}
   296→
   297→	return valid
   298→}

    13→// Type aliases for convenience - use the shared schema types
    14→type (
    15→	SessionData  = schema.SessionData
    16→	ProviderInfo = schema.ProviderInfo
    17→	Exchange     = schema.Exchange
    18→	Message      = schema.Message
    19→	ContentPart  = schema.ContentPart

    21→	Usage        = schema.Usage
