    87→// parseResourceAttributes parses OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES env var into attribute.KeyValue slice.
    88→// Format: "key1=value1,key2=value2"
    89→func parseResourceAttributes() []attribute.KeyValue {
    90→	envVal := os.Getenv("OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES")
    91→	if envVal == "" {
    92→		return nil
    93→	}
    94→
    95→	var attrs []attribute.KeyValue
    96→	pairs := strings.Split(envVal, ",")
    97→	for _, pair := range pairs {
    98→		pair = strings.TrimSpace(pair)
    99→		if pair == "" {
   100→			continue
   101→		}
   102→		kv := strings.SplitN(pair, "=", 2)
   103→		if len(kv) == 2 {
   104→			key := strings.TrimSpace(kv[0])
   105→			value := strings.TrimSpace(kv[1])
   106→			if key != "" {
   107→				attrs = append(attrs, attribute.String(key, value))
   108→			}
   109→		}
   110→	}
   111→	return attrs
   112→}
   113→
   114→// parseEndpoint normalises an OTLP endpoint string into a bare host:port suitable
   115→// for otlptracegrpc.WithEndpoint and a flag indicating whether TLS should be disabled.
   116→//
   117→// Accepted formats:
   118→//
   119→//	"localhost:4317"              → host="localhost:4317",  insecure=true
   120→//	"http://localhost:4317"       → host="localhost:4317",  insecure=true
   121→//	"https://collector.example:4317" → host="collector.example:4317", insecure=false
   122→//	""                            → host=defaultEndpoint,  insecure=true
   123→func parseEndpoint(raw string) (host string, insecure bool) {
   124→	if raw == "" {
   125→		return defaultEndpoint, true
   126→	}
   127→
   128→	u, err := url.Parse(raw)
   129→	if err != nil || u.Host == "" {
   130→		// Not a URL — treat the whole string as host:port (bare address).
   131→		return raw, true
   132→	}
   133→
   134→	// Parsed successfully as a URL with a scheme.
   135→	host = u.Host
   136→	insecure = u.Scheme != "https"
   137→	return host, insecure
   138→}

   140→// Init configures the OTel tracing and metrics subsystem. Thread-safe and idempotent — only the
   141→// first call takes effect. When Enabled is false the global no-op provider remains
   142→// active, so callers can emit spans/events and record metrics safely with zero overhead.
   143→func Init(ctx context.Context, opts Options) error {
   144→	var initErr error
   145→	initOnce.Do(func() {
   146→		if !opts.Enabled {
   147→			telemetryLogger().Info("Telemetry disabled, using no-op provider")
   148→			return
   149→		}
   150→
   151→		// Route OTel SDK errors (export failures, connection issues) through slog
   152→		// so they appear in debug logs alongside our own telemetry messages.
   153→		otel.SetErrorHandler(otel.ErrorHandlerFunc(func(err error) {
   154→			telemetryLogger().Warn("OTel SDK error", "error", err)
   155→		}))
   156→
   157→		serviceName := opts.ServiceName
   158→		if serviceName == "" {
   159→			serviceName = "specstory-cli"
   160→		}
   161→
   162→		// Parse the endpoint to extract a bare host:port for WithEndpoint and
   163→		// determine TLS mode from the scheme. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is
   164→		// conventionally a full URL (e.g. "http://localhost:4317"), but
   165→		// WithEndpoint expects just "host:port".
   166→		host, insecure := parseEndpoint(opts.Endpoint)
   167→
   168→		// Create shared resource for both traces and metrics.
   169→		// Use resource.New() with detectors to pick up OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES env var.
   170→		res, err := resource.New(ctx,
   171→			resource.WithFromEnv(),      // OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and OTEL_SERVICE_NAME
   172→			resource.WithTelemetrySDK(), // telemetry.sdk.* attributes
   173→			resource.WithHost(),         // host.* attributes
   174→			resource.WithAttributes(attribute.String("service.name", serviceName)), // explicit service name (can override env)
   175→		)
   176→		if err != nil {
   177→			initErr = fmt.Errorf("create OTel resource: %w", err)
   178→			return
   179→		}
   180→
   181→		// Log the resource attributes for debugging
   182→		telemetryLogger().Debug("Resource attributes created",
   183→			"attributes", res.Attributes(),
   184→			"OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES", os.Getenv("OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES"),
   185→		)
   186→
   187→		// Initialize tracing
   188→		if err := initTracing(ctx, host, insecure, res); err != nil {
   189→			initErr = err
   190→			return
   191→		}
   192→
   193→		// Initialize metrics
   194→		if err := initMetrics(ctx, host, insecure, res); err != nil {
   195→			// Roll back tracing initialization to avoid half-initialized state
   196→			telemetryLogger().Warn("Metrics init failed, rolling back tracing", "error", err)
   197→			if traceProvider != nil {
   198→				if shutdownErr := traceProvider.Shutdown(ctx); shutdownErr != nil {
   199→					telemetryLogger().Warn("Failed to shutdown trace provider during rollback", "error", shutdownErr)
   200→				}
   201→				traceProvider = nil
   202→				// Use no-op provider instead of nil per OTel documentation
   203→				otel.SetTracerProvider(noop.NewTracerProvider())
   204→			}
   205→			initErr = err
   206→			return
   207→		}
   208→
   209→		metricsEnabled = true
   210→
   211→		// Parse OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and store as common metric attributes.
   212→		// This ensures resource attributes appear as metric tags in backends like Datadog
   213→		// that may not automatically promote resource-level attributes to metric tags.
   214→		commonMetricAttrs = parseResourceAttributes()
   215→		if len(commonMetricAttrs) > 0 {
   216→			telemetryLogger().Debug("Parsed OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES for metrics",
   217→				"count", len(commonMetricAttrs),
   218→				"attributes", commonMetricAttrs,
   219→			)
   220→		}
   221→
   222→		telemetryLogger().Info("Telemetry initialised",
   223→			"endpoint", host,
   224→			"insecure", insecure,
   225→			"serviceName", serviceName,
   226→		)
   227→	})
   228→
   229→	return initErr
   230→}

   232→// initTracing sets up the trace provider and exporter.
   233→func initTracing(ctx context.Context, host string, insecure bool, res *resource.Resource) error {
   234→	exporterOpts := []otlptracegrpc.Option{
   235→		otlptracegrpc.WithEndpoint(host),
   236→	}
   237→	if insecure {
   238→		exporterOpts = append(exporterOpts, otlptracegrpc.WithInsecure())
   239→	}
   240→
   241→	exporter, err := otlptracegrpc.New(ctx, exporterOpts...)
   242→	if err != nil {
   243→		return fmt.Errorf("create OTLP trace exporter: %w", err)
   244→	}
   245→
   246→	traceProvider = sdktrace.NewTracerProvider(
   247→		sdktrace.WithBatcher(exporter),
   248→		sdktrace.WithResource(res),
   249→	)
   250→	otel.SetTracerProvider(traceProvider)
   251→
   252→	return nil
   253→}
   254→
   255→// initMetrics sets up the meter provider, exporter, and metric instruments.
   256→func initMetrics(ctx context.Context, host string, insecure bool, res *resource.Resource) error {

   258→		otlpmetricgrpc.WithEndpoint(host),
   259→	}
   260→	if insecure {
   261→		exporterOpts = append(exporterOpts, otlpmetricgrpc.WithInsecure())
   262→	}
   263→
   264→	exporter, err := otlpmetricgrpc.New(ctx, exporterOpts...)
   265→	if err != nil {
   266→		return fmt.Errorf("create OTLP metric exporter: %w", err)
   267→	}
   268→
   269→	meterProvider = sdkmetric.NewMeterProvider(
   270→		sdkmetric.WithResource(res),
   271→		sdkmetric.WithReader(sdkmetric.NewPeriodicReader(exporter,
   272→			sdkmetric.WithInterval(metricExportInterval),

   274→	)
   275→	otel.SetMeterProvider(meterProvider)
   276→
   277→	meter = meterProvider.Meter("specstory-cli")
   278→
   279→	// Initialize metric instruments
   280→	if err := initMetricInstruments(); err != nil {
   281→		return fmt.Errorf("create metric instruments: %w", err)
   282→	}
   283→
   284→	return nil
   285→}

   418→// Shutdown flushes pending spans/metrics and shuts down both providers.
   419→// Safe to call even when Init was never called or telemetry is disabled.
   420→// For short-lived CLIs, this performs explicit ForceFlush calls before shutdown
   421→// to ensure all data is exported before the process exits.
   422→func Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error {
   423→	var errs []error
   424→
   425→	if traceProvider != nil {
   426→		telemetryLogger().Info("Flushing and shutting down trace provider")
   427→		// ForceFlush ensures all pending spans are exported before shutdown.
   428→		// This is critical for short-lived CLIs that may exit before the
   429→		// periodic exporter has time to run.
   430→		if err := traceProvider.ForceFlush(ctx); err != nil {
   431→			telemetryLogger().Warn("Failed to flush trace provider", "error", err)
   432→		}
   433→		if err := traceProvider.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
   434→			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("shutdown trace provider: %w", err))
   435→		}
   436→	}
   437→
   438→	if meterProvider != nil {
   439→		telemetryLogger().Info("Flushing and shutting down meter provider")
   440→		// ForceFlush ensures all pending metrics are exported before shutdown.
   441→		// The periodic reader has a 10-second interval, so without this,
   442→		// metrics from short CLI runs would never be sent.
   443→		if err := meterProvider.ForceFlush(ctx); err != nil {
   444→			telemetryLogger().Warn("Failed to flush meter provider", "error", err)
   445→		}
   446→		if err := meterProvider.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
   447→			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("shutdown meter provider: %w", err))
   448→		}
   449→	}
   450→
   451→	if len(errs) > 0 {
   452→		return errs[0] // Return first error
   453→	}
   454→	return nil
   455→}
   456→
   457→// ForceFlush explicitly flushes all pending spans and metrics.
   458→// Call this at the end of short-lived commands to ensure data is exported
   459→// before the command returns. Safe to call when telemetry is disabled.
   460→func ForceFlush(ctx context.Context) error {
   461→	var errs []error
   462→
   463→	if traceProvider != nil {
   464→		telemetryLogger().Debug("Force flushing trace provider")
   465→		if err := traceProvider.ForceFlush(ctx); err != nil {
   466→			telemetryLogger().Warn("Failed to force flush trace provider", "error", err)
   467→			errs = append(errs, err)
   468→		}
   469→	}
   470→
   471→	if meterProvider != nil {
   472→		telemetryLogger().Debug("Force flushing meter provider")
   473→		if err := meterProvider.ForceFlush(ctx); err != nil {
   474→			telemetryLogger().Warn("Failed to force flush meter provider", "error", err)
   475→			errs = append(errs, err)
   476→		}
   477→	}
   478→
   479→	if len(errs) > 0 {
   480→		return errs[0]
   481→	}
   482→	return nil
   483→}

   500→// ContextWithSessionTrace returns a context that will cause any spans started
   501→// from it to share the same trace ID (derived deterministically from sessionID).
   502→// This groups all spans for a given session into a single trace, even across
   503→// multiple invocations (e.g., in autosave mode where processSingleSession is
   504→// called repeatedly as the session file grows).
   505→func ContextWithSessionTrace(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) context.Context {
   506→	traceID := traceIDFromSessionID(sessionID)
   507→	spanID := spanIDFromSessionID(sessionID)
   508→
   509→	// Create a SpanContext with both deterministic trace ID and span ID.
   510→	// In OpenTelemetry-Go, a SpanContext is only valid if both TraceID and SpanID
   511→	// are valid. We mark it as Remote so child spans inherit the trace ID.
   512→	sc := trace.NewSpanContext(trace.SpanContextConfig{
   513→		TraceID:    traceID,
   514→		SpanID:     spanID,
   515→		TraceFlags: trace.FlagsSampled, // Ensure it's sampled
   516→		Remote:     true,               // Mark as remote parent
   517→	})
   518→
   519→	// Inject the SpanContext as a remote parent so child spans inherit the trace ID
   520→	return trace.ContextWithRemoteSpanContext(ctx, sc)
   521→}
   522→
   523→// traceIDFromSessionID generates a deterministic 16-byte trace ID from a session ID
   524→// by hashing the session ID with SHA-256 and taking the first 16 bytes.
   525→func traceIDFromSessionID(sessionID string) trace.TraceID {
   526→	hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(sessionID))
   527→	var traceID trace.TraceID
   528→	copy(traceID[:], hash[:16])
   529→	return traceID
   530→}
   531→
   532→// spanIDFromSessionID generates a deterministic 8-byte span ID from a session ID
   533→// by hashing the session ID with SHA-256 and taking bytes 16-24.
   534→// This ensures the span ID is different from the trace ID but still deterministic.
   535→func spanIDFromSessionID(sessionID string) trace.SpanID {
   536→	hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(sessionID))

   539→	return spanID

   119→// parseEndpoint normalises an OTLP endpoint string into a bare host:port suitable
   120→// for otlptracegrpc.WithEndpoint and a flag indicating whether TLS should be disabled.
   121→//
   122→// Accepted formats:
   123→//
   124→//	"localhost:4317"                 → host="localhost:4317",          insecure=true
   125→//	"http://localhost:4317"          → host="localhost:4317",          insecure=true
   126→//	"https://collector.example:4317" → host="collector.example:4317",  insecure=false
   127→func parseEndpoint(raw string) (host string, insecure bool) {
   128→	u, err := url.Parse(raw)
   129→	if err != nil || u.Host == "" {
   130→		// Not a URL — treat the whole string as host:port (bare address).
   131→		return raw, true
   132→	}
   133→
   134→	// Parsed successfully as a URL with a scheme.
   135→	host = u.Host
   136→	insecure = u.Scheme != "https"
   137→	return host, insecure
   138→}
   139→
   140→// Init configures the OTel tracing and metrics subsystem. Thread-safe and idempotent — only the
   141→// first call takes effect. When Enabled is false the global no-op provider remains
   142→// active, so callers can emit spans/events and record metrics safely with zero overhead.
